Fixture trap in group B (benchmarks/darkrp-core/private/harbor/darkrp-release-regressions-v3/tests/suite.lua:47-50 and 57-62): the stand-in's PhysicsInit returns true while GetPhysicsObject returns NULL, a combination the engine does not produce (PhysicsInit succeeding means a physics object exists). An implementation that keys the wake on the result of DarkRP.ValidatedPhysicsInit/PhysicsInit instead of on phys:IsValid() is correct in the real engine but fails both B cases. Control alternative-strict-reading demonstrates this.

Over-constraining observer in group G (benchmarks/darkrp-core/private/harbor/darkrp-release-regressions-v3/tests/suite.lua:140-149): 'the admin must be told something' is detected only by replacing FAdmin.Messages.SendMessage. Feedback sent through ply:PrintMessage/ChatPrint, DarkRP.notify, FAdmin.Messages.ConsoleNotify or a net message is not seen and would fail, although the comment at suite.lua:120-122 says the mechanism is unconstrained. Every neighbouring FAdmin command uses SendMessage, so the natural fix passes.

Group G stubs FAdmin.Access.PlayerHasPrivilege to true and calls entry.callback directly (benchmarks/darkrp-core/private/harbor/darkrp-release-regressions-v3/tests/suite.lua:134-147); a fix placed in the FAdmin command dispatcher (argument validation before the callback is reached) would not be exercised and would fail.
